consequences: Hints in doctor and init name `sati upgrade`. The text inside the git hook runner still says `init --upgrade`, because changing it would mark every project's hooks as out of date. `task claim` with no id keeps claiming the top ready task. fish completion is untested.
context: The owner asked why updating a project needs `sati init --upgrade --yes`. The upgrade only rewrites files this tool manages, and git shows the change, so the question added a flag without adding safety.
decision: `sati upgrade` does the work of `init --upgrade --yes` and never prompts; `--dry-run` previews. `init --upgrade` keeps its prompt and its `--yes` rule. Completions are generated from the command tree at run time. Long output goes through a pager only for a person at a terminal (SATI_PAGER, PAGER, less; PAGER=cat off; none by default on Windows). Rejected: an interactive picker for `task claim`.
title: Terminal follow-ups: `sati upgrade` asks nothing; pager as git; no picker for task claim
